conv.title: Currency converter: foreign currency to TZS
conv.desc: Convert US dollars, euros, pounds and other currencies to Tanzanian shillings and back, using the official rate, the market rate or a named bank's rate.
conv.lead: Choose a currency, an amount and which rate to use. The default is the Bank of Tanzania mean rate.
conv.unavailable: This rate is not available for this currency right now.
conv.basis_note: For a bank, converting foreign currency to shillings uses the bank's buying rate (what it pays you), and shillings to foreign currency uses its selling rate (what you pay). Real transactions can differ: fees, amounts and timing all matter.

banks.title: Bank exchange rates in Tanzania compared
banks.desc: Buying and selling rates and spreads at CRDB, NBC and Stanbic compared with the Bank of Tanzania rate.
banks.lead: Board rates published by banks, with the spread and how far each is from the official Bank of Tanzania mean.
banks.how: Spread = selling rate minus buying rate. A smaller spread is cheaper for you. Only banks that publish rates online in a form we can read automatically are included, so this is not every bank in Tanzania.
banks.cheapest_note: Spread as a percentage of the midpoint of the bank's buying and selling rates. Ties are common: banks often publish identical rates for the US dollar.

method.title: Methodology and sources
method.desc: Where every number comes from, how spread and change are calculated, and how to cite this data.
method.lead: Every number on this site comes from an official or market source, is stored with the time it was read, and is never typed in by hand.
method.src.bot: Official indicative buying, selling and mean rates for about 38 currencies against the shilling.
method.cad.bot: Checked several times a day. The Bank of Tanzania publishes once per business day.
method.src.mid: A global reference rate (units of each currency per US dollar), converted to TZS per unit.
method.src.crdb: Buying and selling board rates published on the bank's website.
method.src.nbc: Telegraphic-transfer (T.T.) buying and selling rates from the bank's published rate sheet (PDF).
method.cad.nbc: Checked several times a day; the bank updates its sheet about once a day.
method.src.stanbic: Buying and selling rates from the bank's published indicative rate sheet (PDF).
method.cad.stanbic: Checked several times a day; the bank updates its sheet about once a day.
method.indicative: Bank of Tanzania rates are reference rates calculated from market activity. They are not a price at which anyone is obliged to deal. Real transactions at banks and bureaux de change vary with the amount, fees, the time of day and the counterparty.
method.mean_d: The Bank of Tanzania mean is the figure it publishes, shown unchanged. It is the midpoint of its buying and selling rates.
method.spread_d: Selling rate minus buying rate, in TZS, and as a percentage of the midpoint of the two.
method.change_d: The latest Bank of Tanzania mean compared with the most recent published mean on or before 1, 7 and 30 days earlier, on 31 December of the previous year (year to date), and one year earlier.
method.dir_d: All rates are shillings per one unit of foreign currency. A rising rate means the shilling weakened; a falling rate means it strengthened.
method.gap_t: Market rate against the official rate
method.gap_d: The latest mid-market rate minus the latest Bank of Tanzania mean, in TZS and %. The market feed is a global aggregate and can be stale or wrong for a thinly traded currency like the shilling, so clearly unreliable days are excluded.
method.best_d: The highest buying rate (best if you sell foreign currency) and the lowest selling rate (best if you buy it) among banks whose rate was read in the last 36 hours.
method.bot_p1: The Bank of Tanzania publishes its indicative table once per business day. Its page can show a new date with the previous day's numbers before the new table is out; we mark those readings and keep showing the last genuine table.
method.bot_p2: Older rates come from the Bank of Tanzania's own history search. That table repeats the last rate over weekends and holidays, and its date labels can differ from the live table by a day, so we keep a date only when its full table differs from the day before. For the most recent days the history table can lag behind the live table.
method.banks_p: Banks publish board rates on their websites, some as PDF rate sheets. We read them automatically. They are indicative and can differ at the counter. Where a bank publishes several rate types we use its telegraphic-transfer buying and selling rates.
method.quality_p: Automated checks reject zero or negative rates and rates where buying exceeds selling, and hold back any live value that moves more than 3% from the previous one. We found {n} clearly wrong points in source data (for example decimal-point typos, and a stale market feed in December 2024). They are left out of charts and calculations but never deleted from the stored record.
method.limits_p: This is a data service, not financial advice. Rates can be delayed or wrong at the source. Check the rate with your bank or the Bank of Tanzania before you transact.
method.cite_p: Name the source and the date you read it. A suggested form:
method.cite_text: Bank of Tanzania indicative exchange rates, via {site} ({url}), accessed {date}.
method.data_p: The data behind every page is available as JSON and CSV. Please credit this site when you use it.
